validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED by 2 independent trade sources that name this exact pipeline, which the sheet's own citations do NOT. The row's only wiki citations are generic OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB2012 p.75, ASB2017 p.136, ASB2013 p.79); all fetch 200 but NONE contain 'Haradh' or 'Uthman' — country-level statistics tables, not evidence for this pipeline (an existence red flag on the sheet's sourcing, resolved by external evidence). Independent naming: (1) OGJ 'Saudi Aramco commissions Haradh GOSP-3' (the current Start [ref]) states 'The gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah has a 1,140 hp motor-driven gas compressor and two 10,460 hp compressors' and dates GOSP-3 commissioning to 14 Feb 2006 — supports the gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah AND StartYear1=2006. (2) MEED 'Hawiyah pipeline programme progresses' names 'the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1)' and a 48-inch inlet/outlet line tying into it — corroborates the line's identity and 48-in diameter. CLASSIFICATION — correct: a gas transmission trunk moving Haradh-area gas north to the Uthmaniyah Gas Plant; not gathering/plant-internal/oil. DUPLICATE — checked vs roster and GulfPub: NOT a duplicate. The offshore-technology 'Haradh-Hawiyah Gas' (450 km, 36 in, 2024 start) is the newer Haradh & Hawiyah Gas Compression project, a different line; P1907 'Haradh-3-Uthmaniya' (124 km, 24/32 in) is a distinct parallel/increment line; P1915 'Hawiyah-Uthmniyah' (47 km) and P1917-19 'Haradh Khuff-Hawiyah' (43 km) are shorter distinct segments. No GulfPub feature matches (GulfPub SA-gas roster has no Haradh-Uthmaniyah entry). ATTRIBUTION — Owner=Saudi Aramco correct (Aramco field/plant infrastructure); Fuel=Gas correct; region Eastern Province correct; endpoints Haradh (Al-Ahsa) -> Uthmaniyah correct. SPEC — Diameter 48 in corroborated by MEED. StartYear 2006 corroborated by OGJ. Capacity blank (unknown, not forced). CAVEAT: LengthKnown 140.01 km (87 mi) has NO independent corroboration — no external source gives a length for the HDUG main line; treat as an unverified GEM estimate, not a concern-level disagreement (no source contradicts it either).

fills.researcher_notes: Operating since 2006 (OGJ, GOSP-3 gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah commissioned Feb 2006); still an in-service tie-in for the Hawiyah NGL programme (MEED). Two independent sources.
OGJ describes it as 'the gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah'; MEED calls it the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line. Natural gas transmission.
MEED ties a 48-inch line to the Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line (HDUG-1). Single strong independent source explicitly linking 48 in to this line; no conflicting figure found.
Gas originates from the Haradh increment / Haradh GOSP-3 development (OGJ); routed north to Uthmaniyah. FuelSource=Haradh consistent with the source article.

Haradh (in Al-Ahsa governorate, Eastern Province) -> Uthmaniyah (central Ghawar, Eastern Province). Both endpoints named in OGJ ('gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah', Haradh GOSP-3) and MEED (Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line).
Saudi Aramco field/plant infrastructure (Haradh & Hawiyah/Uthmaniyah gas complexes). Both sources attribute the works to Saudi Aramco. 100% Aramco.

No independent source gives a length for the HDUG main line (MEED only gives the separate 25 km / 48-in inlet-outlet tie-in). LengthKnown 87 mi / 140.01 km is an unverified GEM estimate; left UNRESOLVED rather than paired with a non-supporting ref. Geographically plausible for a Haradh->Hawiyah->Uthmaniyah corridor but not corroborated.

routes.start_name: Haradh Gas Plant area, Haradh (Al-Ahsa), Eastern Province
routes.end_name: Uthmaniyah Gas Plant, central Ghawar, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly NNW along the eastern flank of the Ghawar field from the Haradh area (southern Ghawar, Al-Ahsa governorate) north through Hawiyah to the Uthmaniyah Gas Plant in central Ghawar. Corridor is well-bounded by the Ghawar facility chain (Haradh -> Hawiyah -> Uthmaniyah); ~140 km along-route is consistent with this path. Endpoint coordinates are approximate (defensible from the named towns/plants Haradh, Hawiyah, Uthmaniyah), NOT surveyed pipeline vertices.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from OGJ (gas pipeline from Haradh GOSP-3 to Uthmaniyah) and MEED (Haradh-Uthmaniyah gas line, tied into the Hawiyah NGL plant, placing Hawiyah on/near the route). Coordinates are approximate, derived from the named settlements/plants (Haradh ~24.15N/49.10E, Hawiyah ~24.75N/49.30E, Uthmaniyah ~25.10N/49.30E); no coordinate was fabricated at higher precision than the named place supports. A human routes-repo branch should refine against imagery of the Ghawar facility corridor.

summary: P1905 Haradh-Uthmaniya (HDUG-1) confirmed real + gas transmission, not a duplicate; sheet's OPEC-ASB citations don't name it, replaced by OGJ+MEED (existence high, 48-in diameter medium, 2006 start high).
